summary: Baileys fork aliases `libsignal` to a third-party scope pinned to floating `latest`
details: @lendxntaa/baileys is a fork of the Baileys WhatsApp client that declares `"libsignal": "npm:@bellaxchuu/libsignal-node@latest"` in package.json. The `libsignal` module id is loaded on the crypto/signal path of the WhatsApp client, so `require('libsignal')` inside this package resolves to code published under the unrelated `@bellaxchuu` scope, pinned to the mutable `latest` tag with no version and no integrity metadata. Every `npm install` can resolve to different bytes chosen by whoever controls that scope, and those bytes execute in-process whenever a consumer of this package uses the WA client. Package metadata further reduces reviewability: `homepage` and `repository.url` both point at a Telegram channel (`https://t.me/lendd3`) rather than a source repository, and the tarball ships a ~130 KB `lib/antiban.js` bundle not present in upstream Baileys.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
